chapters.title: Space Telescope Engineering
chapters.scope:
- Why go to space: atmospheric absorption windows across the spectrum (computed schematic figure of atmospheric transmission/altitude needed vs wavelength using approximate data you cite), seeing vs diffraction, sky background and thermal emission (computed Planck curves showing why infrared telescopes must be cold: 300 K vs 40 K vs 7 K telescope emission vs a faint source).
- Optics: diffraction limit 1.22λ/D (computed figure: angular resolution vs aperture for UV/optical/IR/sub-mm and the Airy pattern), telescope designs (Cassegrain, Ritchey–Chrétien, three-mirror anastigmat, off-axis), segmented and deployable mirrors (JWST 18 segments, wavefront sensing and control), mirror materials (Zerodur, ULE, beryllium, SiC) and lightweighting, X-ray grazing-incidence (Wolter) optics, coded masks and pair-conversion telescopes for gamma rays, coronagraphs and starshades.
- Detectors: CCDs, CMOS, HgCdTe (H2RG/H4RG), Si:As BIB arrays, bolometers, microcalorimeters (XRISM Resolve), CZT, quantum efficiency and noise; computed photon-budget / SNR vs magnitude figure for different apertures and exposure times.
- Thermal design: passive cooling, sunshields (JWST five-layer shield), cryocoolers (MIRI 7 K), stray light control, contamination control.
- Pointing and stability: fine guidance sensors, reaction-wheel jitter and isolation, Hubble's gyroscopes and one-gyro mode since 2024 (VERIFY), drift scanning; a computed pointing-jitter vs image-blur figure.
- Orbits for telescopes: LEO (Hubble), HEO (Chandra), Sun–Earth L2 halo orbits (JWST, Euclid, Roman — Roman launched 30 Aug 2026, see notes), Earth-trailing (Spitzer, Kepler); trade-offs for thermal stability, data rates, servicing.
- Servicing and assembly: Hubble servicing missions SM1–SM4, future in-space assembly of large apertures (link to Chapter 40).
- Data: volumes and downlink (JWST Ka-band ~28 Mbit/s and ~57 GB/day — VERIFY), pipelines, archives (MAST).
- Worked examples: resolution of a 6.5 m telescope at 2 µm; photon count from a 25th-magnitude star; sunshield temperature drop.
- AI box: ML in wavefront control, scheduling and data reduction (Chapter 46).

chapters.title: Great Observatories and Deep-Space Telescopes
chapters.scope:
- NASA's Great Observatories: Hubble (1990; spherical aberration and COSTAR; servicing; one-gyro operations; status and reboost discussions — VERIFY), Compton (1991–2000), Chandra (1999; budget threats 2025–26 — VERIFY), Spitzer (2003–2020).
- JWST (launched 25 Dec 2021): design summary, commissioning, science highlights (record-distance galaxies e.g. JADES-GS-z14-0 and any newer records — VERIFY; exoplanet atmospheres e.g. CO2 in WASP-39b; the K2-18b debate; early black holes), status 2026.
- Survey and astrophysics missions (VERIFY all dates and statuses as of Oct 2026): Kepler and TESS (exoplanet counts — VERIFY confirmed exoplanet total ~6,000), Gaia (science operations ended Jan 2025, passivated Mar 2025; DR4 timing), Euclid (2023; Q1 release Mar 2025), Roman (launched 30 Aug 2026), SPHEREx and PUNCH (Mar 2025), XRISM, IXPE, Fermi, Swift (orbit decay/reboost plans — VERIFY), NuSTAR, Einstein Probe, SVOM, eROSITA, Chinese Xuntian/CSST (launch — VERIFY), PLATO (launch — VERIFY), Ariel, NewAthena, LISA (adopted 2024), Habitable Worlds Observatory concept; CMB missions COBE, WMAP, Planck; radio (RadioAstron), and the James Webb successor plans.
- A big table of space observatories: band, aperture, orbit, launch, status 2026.
- Computed figures: electromagnetic-spectrum coverage chart of missions (bar segments by wavelength range), observatory Gantt chart 1990–2035, aperture vs launch year, exoplanet discoveries per year by method (from NASA Exoplanet Archive counts you verify, or a carefully cited summary), and a figure illustrating cosmological look-back time vs redshift (compute with a flat ΛCDM model H0=67.7, Ωm=0.31).
- Photos: Hubble on-orbit, JWST mirror, iconic images (Pillars of Creation, deep fields), Chandra, Roman, etc. from the NASA library.
- Worked examples: look-back time to z = 14; light-travel time and distance concepts; TESS transit depth for an Earth-size planet around a Sun-like star.
- AI box: ML for transient classification, exoplanet vetting, galaxy morphology (Chapter 46).

chapters.title: In-Space Servicing, Assembly and Manufacturing
chapters.scope:
- Definitions (ISAM / OSAM) and why it matters (life extension, upgrade, debris removal, large structures, new products).
- History of servicing: Skylab repairs, Solar Max (1984), Intelsat 603 rescue (1992), Hubble servicing missions, ISS assembly and maintenance, Orbital Express (2007), Northrop Grumman MEV-1 (2020) and MEV-2 (2021) life extension, Mission Robotic Vehicle and Mission Extension Pods (status — VERIFY), NASA OSAM-1 cancellation (2024), China's Shijian-21 (2022 GEO tug) and Shijian-25 refuelling of SJ-21 in 2025 (VERIFY), Astroscale ELSA-d (2021), ADRAS-J (2024 close approach to an H-IIA upper stage — VERIFY range) and ADRAS-J2, ClearSpace, Starfish Space Otter (VERIFY), Orbit Fab, Starship propellant transfer demonstration (VERIFY 2026 status), Katalyst / Swift reboost mission (VERIFY).
- Engineering: rendezvous and proximity operations (relative motion, Clohessy–Wiltshire already in Chapter 21 — cross-reference, but include a computed V-bar/R-bar approach figure), capture of unprepared clients (tumbling objects, grapple fixtures, docking to launch-adapter rings), robotic arms and tools, refuelling interfaces (RAFTI, ASSIST), standards (CONFERS), safety, legal issues.
- In-space assembly: ISS truss assembly, large antennas/telescopes, robotic assembly demonstrations, modular spacecraft; computed figure comparing deployable vs assembled aperture sizes vs launcher fairing.
- In-space manufacturing: ISS 3D printers (Made In Space 2014; ESA metal printer 2024 — VERIFY), ZBLAN fibre, protein crystals, bioprinting, Varda Space Industries capsules (W-1 2024, W-2/W-3/W-4 — VERIFY), semiconductors, space-based solar power demos (Caltech SSPD-1/MAPLE 2023).
- Economics: value of a GEO satellite-year vs servicing price; computed figure of life extension value vs propellant remaining; debris-removal economics.
- Worked examples: Δv and propellant for a tug to dock with and move a GEO satellite to graveyard orbit; CW relative motion for an approach; transfer of propellant mass for a lunar Starship (number of tanker flights estimate with clearly stated assumptions).
- AI box: autonomous rendezvous and capture, vision-based pose estimation (Chapter 45/46).

chapters.title: Space Resources and Asteroid Mining
chapters.scope:
- Why space resources: the 'gear ratio' of launching mass from Earth vs producing it in space (computed figure of mass leverage of lunar-derived propellant for missions to lunar orbit/Mars using Δv values you state).
- What is out there: lunar polar water ice (LCROSS ~5.6 % water by mass in Cabeus ejecta; LRO/LAMP/Diviner/M3 evidence; Chandrayaan; current estimates — VERIFY), lunar regolith oxygen (~40–45 % by mass), metals (Fe, Ti, Al), KREEP, helium-3 (realistic assessment), Mars water ice and CO2 atmosphere, asteroid types (C, S, M) and compositions; Psyche; near-Earth asteroid accessibility (computed figure of Δv distribution — you may use a simple Shoemaker–Helin style estimate with stated method).
- ISRU processes with diagrams: water extraction (heating, sublimation capture), electrolysis, hydrogen reduction of ilmenite, carbothermal reduction, molten regolith electrolysis, molten salt (FFC Cambridge), Sabatier and solid-oxide electrolysis on Mars (MOXIE results 2021–23: 122 g O2), regolith construction (sintering, 3D printing, ICON/Project Olympus), energy requirements (computed figure: energy per kg water from regolith at various ice concentrations).
- Prospecting missions: VIPER revived (Blue Origin 2027), PRIME-1 drill on IM-2 (2025), Lunar Trailblazer (lost 2025), Chang'e 7 (2027), Chandrayaan, LUPEX (ISRO–JAXA), ESA PROSPECT (VERIFY statuses).
- Asteroid mining companies: Planetary Resources and Deep Space Industries (rise and fall), AstroForge (Brokkr-1 2023, Odin lost after IM-2 rideshare 2025 — VERIFY, Vestri plans), Karman+, TransAstra; economics (market price collapse when supply increases).
- Law and policy: Outer Space Treaty (1967) Article II, Moon Agreement (1979), US CSLCA (2015), Luxembourg (2017), UAE, Japan (2021) laws, Artemis Accords (76 signatories — see notes), UN COPUOS working group on space resources, NASA's 2020 regolith purchase contracts.
- Worked examples: oxygen from ilmenite yield per tonne of regolith; energy to extract water from 5 % ice regolith; mass leverage of lunar propellant for a lunar-orbit tanker.
- AI box: ML for resource mapping from orbital spectra, autonomous mining robots (Chapter 46).

chapters.title: Advanced Propulsion
chapters.scope:
- The rocket equation's tyranny: why higher exhaust velocity matters (computed figure of mass ratio vs Δv for chemical, nuclear thermal, electric, fusion exhaust velocities).
- Advanced electric propulsion: high-power Hall thrusters (AEPS for Gateway PPE — VERIFY status), gridded ion (NEXT-C on DART), magnetoplasmadynamic, VASIMR, field-emission; power-limited trajectories: computed figure of trip time vs specific power (kW/kg) for a Mars mission; solar vs nuclear power.
- Nuclear thermal propulsion: Rover/NERVA history (Isp ~850–900 s), reactor physics basics, HALEU fuels, DARPA/NASA DRACO (cancelled 2025 — VERIFY), China/Russia efforts; Mars transit-time comparison (computed).
- Nuclear electric propulsion and fission power (Kilopower/KRUSTY 2018, Fission Surface Power — VERIFY 2025–26 directives on a lunar reactor).
- Solar sails: IKAROS (2010), LightSail 2 (2019–22), NASA ACS3 (2024 — VERIFY results), NEA Scout (lost on Artemis I), Solar Cruiser concepts; physics of radiation pressure (computed figure: characteristic acceleration vs areal density at 1 AU), electric sails and magnetic sails.
- Beamed energy and interstellar: Breakthrough Starshot laser sail concept (light pressure, gram-scale chips, ~0.2c), its physics and challenges (computed figure of sail acceleration and velocity under a 100 GW laser with stated parameters), Project Daedalus/Icarus fusion concepts, antimatter (production limits), fusion propulsion concepts (Direct Fusion Drive — VERIFY status).
- Air-breathing and combined-cycle: scramjets (X-43A Mach 9.6, X-51A), SABRE/Reaction Engines (administration Oct 2024 — see notes), rotating detonation engines (JAXA sounding-rocket flight 2021; NASA RDRE tests — VERIFY), and spaceplane implications (link Chapter 10).
- Propellantless and exotic: tethers (electrodynamic, momentum exchange), EmDrive/'reactionless' claims (explain why they failed tests), warp drives (physics reality check).
- A comparison table: Isp, thrust, TRL, power source, examples.
- Worked examples: Mars transit with NTP vs chemical; time for a solar sail to spiral from 1 AU; Starshot laser power and acceleration distance.
- AI box: ML in plasma thruster design and control, mission optimisation (Chapter 47).
